change: Stop claiming useful suffix work after a parallel source-audit failure. Keep every launched job joined and select the earliest manifest-index failure, not the fastest failure.
reasoning: Atomic monotonically increasing claim indices mean all indices earlier than a failing job have already been claimed. They continue, and may lower the first-failure index. Later unscheduled work cannot change the reported failure. A job racing the failure check can already be in flight and remains joined. No partial census is returned as success.

tests.coverage: Exact ordered census versus independent frozen scanner, real compiler source mutations, serial and 2/3/4-worker parity, manifest-priority errors, parser/preprocessor/offset failures, timeout, bounded queue liveness, absence of unnecessary suffix compiler launch after two decisive failures.
tests.red_control: Removed only the new first_failed guard, rebuilt, and ran queue contracts. Failed in 3.70 seconds with compiler suffix launched after a decisive failure. Restored guard and reran both suites successfully.

performance_claim: Avoids unnecessary remaining compiler work on failed audits. No measured successful full-audit speedup claimed; the approximately 153-second successful audit bottleneck remains.
qualification_reuse: No layout, schematic, rendering, audit visitor or acceptance policy changes. Reuse both-board qualification from 2026-10-08-multiscale-outline-qualification.json for unchanged generation code; this is not a new full-board run.
